tools.name: create_list
tools.description: Saves list-shaped content as a ListDrop list the user can keep, check off, and share: an itinerary, a reading or watch list, a packing list, gift ideas, an apartment or job-search shortlist, a step-by-step plan, a checklist. tools.name: get_list
tools.description: Returns a PUBLIC ListDrop list as markdown (title, items, notes, links), given its URL (https://www.listdrop.co/l/<id>/…) or bare id. Private lists are never readable.

tools.name: my_lists
tools.description: Returns the connected user's own lists (titles, visibility, item counts, URLs), private ones included. Requires a connected ListDrop account (OAuth, lists:read scope); without one the server answers 401.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Sends a message to the ListDrop team when the user asks to report a problem, request a feature, or give feedback about ListDrop. A person reads every message. No account needed. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_list" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_list, get_list, my_lists · Private data: create_list, get_list, my_lists, send_feedback · Public sink: create_list, send_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_list, get_list, my_lists · Private data: create_list, get_list, my_lists, send_feedback · Public sink: create_list, send_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
